answer:
Based on the analysis performed on your uploaded `dem.tif` file:

## Mean Slope
The mean slope of the 30 m DEM is **5.75 degrees** (median 5.82°, range 0.57°–5.82°). This was computed using Horn's method (the GDAL-standard 3×3 window slope algorithm) applied to the DEM in its native UTM 16N projection, so the gradient is measured in true metres.

## Watershed Area
The watershed draining to the outlet at 40.04950° N, 88.26302° W (UTM 16N x=392265, y=4434015) has an area of **15.85 km²**.

**Method:** I used pysheds to fill depressions, compute D8 flow direction and flow accumulation, snap the outlet to the nearest flow cell (it snapped to UTM 392250, 4434030, within one 30 m cell of the given point), and delineate the contributing catchment. The catchment contains **17,613 cells × 900 m² = 15,851,700 m² = 15.85 km²**. The polygonized watershed (reprojected to WGS84) is on your interactive map as the layer **"Watershed draining to outlet (40.0495N, 88.2630W)"** — you can pan, zoom and click it. Its WGS84 extent is lon −88.290 to −88.237, lat 40.049 to 40.082.

**Tool note:** The `terrain_derivative` tool failed to produce a usable slope — it reported a mean slope of 0.0° and a nonsensical ground resolution of ~3,340,000 m/pixel instead of the DEM's true 30 m, so I computed the slope directly in code with Horn's method instead. The watershed area was likewise computed in code with pysheds (the polygonization step of that library hit a rasterio dtype bug, which I worked around by tracing the catchment boundary with scikit-image's contour finder).
